Breaking: Bye-Bye, Beige! This 517-Square-Foot Apartment Became a Creative Retreat Full of Light and Color

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “My previous home was dominated by shades of beige,” Jaco Kroon indicates.
  • A vase by ceramist Pol Chambost brings contrast to the table.
  • Sources indicate that “I’d seen a few articles about Elza Wandler’s home and immediately thought: That’s exactly the kind of environment I want: creative, personal, and full of objects that tell stories,” Kroon recalls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“My previous home was dominated by shades of beige,” Jaco Kroon indicates. “And it no longer suited me.” After a career in marketing, Kroon decided to head in a different direction and devote himself to a new creative pursuit: designing furniture for pets. He found the perfect setting for this fresh start in a 517-square-foot apartment in Amsterdam. Together with Elza Wandler, a designer and founder of her eponymous accessory brand, he created an interior that reflects his evolving vision. “I wanted a place that underscores my new direction—a more colorful, more creative, and more surprising home,” explains Kroon.

A vase by ceramist Pol Chambost brings contrast to the table.

Sources indicate that “I’d seen a few articles about Elza Wandler’s home and immediately thought: That’s exactly the kind of environment I want: creative, personal, and full of objects that tell stories,” Kroon recalls. What began as creative interest soon developed into a friendship. During a lunch together in the designer’s garden, the two hit it off right away. In addition to their passion for interior design, they also share a love of dogs—they both own poodles.

It has been revealed that as Kroon got to know Wandler’s home better, he was particularly struck by the fact that every object had its own unique character. They wanted to create a similar atmosphere in his apartment, which led to a close creative collaboration in which they both contributed their ideas and visions. For Kroon, his home soon became more than just a place to live: “While the work was underway, I was developing my own line of pet furniture and realized just how much the fresh interior was influencing my creative work as well.”.

Jaco Kroon’s love for animals has come to shape his career. He’s seen here with his faithful toy poodle, Elio.

According to recent reports, the biggest challenge of the project was making the best use of the limited space. The 517-square-foot apartment combines a kitchen, living room, dining area, and sleeping area without feeling cramped or having to make any sacrifices. According to Wandler, the key was to view the spaces as a cohesive ecosystem: “In such small spaces, every single object interacts with the others. Even a four-inch-tall vase can completely alter the balance of a room.”.

The bedroom is decorated in shades of salmon, with custom cabinets framing the bed. The wallpaper is by Kelly Wearstler. Wall sconces by Contain and the bedding is by Bonsoirs.

This gave rise to the project’s motto: “Every item must be a Beyoncé”—that’s how Wandler and Kroon jokingly describe their design philosophy. It’s their way of expressing the idea that every piece should bring its own personality and presence to the home without disrupting the harmony of the environment. The color scheme also follows this principle with intense yet carefully coordinated tones—such as the eggplant in the kitchen and the warm, velvety salmon pink in the bedroom—paired with textured woods, vintage fabrics, and custom details. “At first, the idea of a burgundy-violet kitchen really put me off,” Kroon admits with a smile. “But the further we got into the project, the more I felt my horizons expanding.”.

A blue bowl by Wandler x SolidNature and a ceramic basket by Ferm Living add splashes of color to the burgundy kitchen. The art on the wall is by Laura de Wilde.

One distinctive feature of the project is the interplay between functionality and aesthetics: Practical solutions blend so naturally into the design that they are barely recognizable as such at first glance. The historic Amsterdam townhouse, with its large windows, had very little storage space. That’s why Wandler took advantage of nearly every opportunity to create additional storage solutions. Custom cabinets frame the bed like an architectural backdrop, while the TV disappears into a specially designed piece of furniture made of zebrawood.

“Elza has turned what would normally be a purely functional piece of furniture into something beautiful. She even convinced me to hide the TV behind the doors of a zebrawood cabinet!” jokes Kroon. “Everything seems to have been designed for aesthetic reasons, but in fact, every element is tailored to make optimal use of the available space.” The decision to use zebrawood also follows this philosophy: Its striking grain lends the interior a vertical dynamism and makes the room appear more spacious. “I wanted to use the wood to create movement and depth,” explains Wandler. “In a small room, you always have to consider how to increase the sense of space.”.

In a recent development, colorful accents, such as the stool by Rutger de Regt, make a bold statement in the interior. The vase is by India Mahdavi and the sculpture on the wall is by Floor Merjenburgh.

As is often the case with Wandler’s projects, restored vintage pieces, contemporary design, and works by young artists all find a place side by side here. The large vintage sofa was completely reupholstered, while the artwork and decorative pieces come from a network of emerging designers and artists supported by the designer through Kamer—her curatorial platform dedicated to collectible design.

The dark wood of the floor complements the chocolate-brown armchair by Norr11.

“It’s important to me that I feel happy in my home,” notes Kroon. “And that it stimulates creativity.” Wandler sought to create this feeling through her selection of artwork and a carefully coordinated lighting design. The latter plays a central role in the living concept: Since the apartment faces multiple directions, the natural light changes constantly throughout the day, causing colors and materials to appear different depending on the time. This creates the impression that this small apartment was conceived as a place that evolves and can accompany personal transformation; it embraces fresh ideas, new ambitions, and new identities. “The greatest compliment,” Wandler concludes, “was when Jaco remarked to me, ‘Now I feel like I’m finally living as the version of myself that I want to become.’”.

According to recent reports, the dining area, with a table from Westwing, is connected to the living room. The vintage sofa by Cini Boeri for Arflex has been reupholstered; the vase in front of the window is by l’Objet.

#76041. Honda’s $2,000 electric moped is a winner. So why can’t Americans buy it?

📖 Baca

Honda’s $2,000 electric moped is a winner. So why can’t Americans buy it?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that honda has been steadily expanding its electric motorcycle lineup, but one of its most interesting new models isn’t a flashy high-performance machine.
  • Unfortunately, that’s probably not happening anytime soon.
  • It has been revealed that we first covered the Honda UC3 earlier this year when the manufacturer confirmed plans to launch the electric scooter in Thailand and Vietnam.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that honda has been steadily expanding its electric motorcycle lineup, but one of its most interesting new models isn’t a flashy high-performance machine. It’s a modest little electric scooter called the Honda UC3, and with prices now dipping close to $2,000 in local markets, it’s the kind of affordable electric two-wheeler that many Americans would probably love to get their hands on.

Unfortunately, that’s probably not happening anytime soon.

It has been revealed that we first covered the Honda UC3 earlier this year when the manufacturer confirmed plans to launch the electric scooter in Thailand and Vietnam. Designed as an electric equivalent to a 110cc gasoline-powered scooter, the UC3 is built for practical everyday transportation rather than weekend joyrides.

But don’t let its modest appearance fool you. The UC3 packs a 6 kW (8 hp) electric motor capable of reaching approximately 50 mph (80 km/h), making it more than capable of handling typical urban commuting.

Its 3.2 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery provides up to 76 miles (122 km) of range under WMTC testing. Unlike Honda’s other electric scooters that use removable batteries, the UC3 has a permanently installed battery that charges directly on the bike.

There’s also a full-color TFT display, smartphone connectivity, three riding modes, reverse gear, and a generous 26-liter under-seat storage compartment.

And perhaps most importantly, it comes from Honda, a tech giant with decades of experience building reliable, affordable motorcycles.

The UC3 originally launched in Vietnam with prices starting around 78.5 million Vietnamese dong, or roughly $3,000. However, recent reports from Vietnamese dealerships show incentives bringing prices down to around 54 million dong, equivalent to approximately $2,100.

That’s a pretty compelling price for a 50 mph (80 km/h) electric scooter from one of the world’s largest motorcycle manufacturers.

But despite its appeal, Honda hasn’t declared any plans to bring the UC3 to the United States.

And frankly, I wouldn’t hold my breath.

Sources indicate that in much of Southeast Asia, scooters are everyday transportation, with millions of riders using them for commuting, shopping, and practically everything else. In the US, motorcycles are much more commonly recreational vehicles, and the market for small, practical scooters is comparatively tiny.

In a recent development, I'm hoping scooters like this take over the world, the sooner the better. Anyone who's travelled in any cities in Asian, India, or most of Europe, there's always a constant background whine of 2-stroke scooters, day and night.

Industry observers note that I would have thought these kinds of markets would have already transitioned to EV - in addition to the annoying sound, those 2-stroke engines spew out an order of magnitude more pollution than most ICE vehicles. I guess it's been a cost glitch - this scooter should be cheap enough to take over the world.

Add in the costs of US regulatory certification, establishing parts and service support, and navigating a market where many buyers expect motorcycles to handle highway speeds, and the business case becomes considerably less attractive.

That’s unfortunate, because the UC3 looks like exactly the kind of electric two-wheeler that could make a real difference in American cities.

It’s affordable, practical, fast enough for most city streets, and backed by a manufacturer that isn’t going anywhere.

Now if only Honda would give Americans a chance to buy one.

According to recent reports, sky’s stUSDS lending vault had $60,484 worth of USDS available for immediate withdrawals at 17:50 UTC on Nov. 20, about 0.04% of the vault’s $161.6 million in total assets, according to Spark.

Spark’s dashboard highlighted about $161.5 million in USDS out on loan at the time, and those loans account for nearly all of the vault’s reported value.

Industry observers note that A holder could redeem only from the portion available in USDS. For example, a saver with $100,000 worth of stUSDS could not have redeemed that entire position directly at the time of the reading, even if nobody else withdrew first.

Savers deposit USDS and receive stUSDS tokens representing their position, and the pool lends USDS to borrowers who put up SKY tokens as collateral. Spark’s dashboard displayed a 29.74% annual percentage yield at the time.

Sky explains that the yield varies with lending conditions. Funds in use earn a rate tied to what borrowers pay, and unused USDS earns the Sky Savings Rate.

The Spark reading measures withdrawal liquidity across the entire vault.

Larger direct withdrawals may have to wait for more USDS to enter the lending pool.

Industry observers note that the withdrawal figure is a point-in-time reading. The diagram highlights possible inflows without estimating their timing or amount.

Sources indicate that divide the $60,484 of withdrawal liquidity by $161,583,152 of total vault assets and multiply by 100. The result is 0.03743%, rounded to 0.04%. The connectors show possible sources of liquidity described by Sky.

Sources indicate that the withdrawal figure is a point-in-time reading. The diagram shows possible inflows without estimating their timing or amount.

Recent findings suggest that when borrowers repay, the USDS they return can become available for withdrawals. New deposits can also add USDS to the pool before borrowers pay down their loans.

When nearly all of the pool is already lent out, a holder may have to wait for more USDS to come in before redeeming their full position.

Sky says the module has no mechanism to liquidate borrowers early to free up funds for depositors. The loan collateral is in SKY, while holders redeem their stUSDS shares for USDS available in the vault.

Sky Frontier Foundation separately stated on Nov. 20 that people exchanged more than $2 billion of USDS for USDC the previous day through Sky’s Peg Stability Module. The foundation said the facility continued to swap the two stablecoins at a one-to-one rate during the Nov. 19 activity.

The swap facility serves customers who already have USDS to exchange. An stUSDS holder using the vault would first have to redeem for USDS before using that route to get USDC.

The amount a vault depositor can withdraw depends on how much USDS is in the lending pool when the redemption is attempted.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Canada’s government wants to make it easier for citizens to drive electric, and they’re putting more than $4 billion in funding for electricity infrastructure and grid modernization that includes more than 55,000 upcoming EV chargers.

The proposed federal budget set aside $4 billion (CAD) for grid improvements, with a $~635 million carveout specifically for EV charging infrastructure with $587 million of that set aside to renew the Zero-Emission Vehicle Infrastructure Program (ZEVIP), which funds the development of new public EV charging stations.

In a recent development, “The charging industry is really encouraged by the multi-year investment in the budget,” explains Travis Allan, president and CEO of the Canadian Charging Infrastructure Council (CCIC) told Electric Autonomy. “We’ll be looking to make sure that we have great programs in place to deal with the barriers faced by people living in condos and apartments, public fast charging, which needs to cover major corridors and metropolitan areas, and then also charging for fleets and medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, which make up a major share of transportation emissions.”.

According to recent reports, the rest of the $4 billion will be spent on electricity infrastructure expansion over the next 10 years, starting in 2027 and running through 2036. Because it’s Canada where nearly 60% of electrical generation already comes from renewable hydro and wind power, renewable energy is a de-facto priority, with carveouts for the Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program, newly introduced data and modeling efforts to guide grid planning, and $1.6 billion to modernize power systems in northern and remote communities.

The charging infrastructure program highlighted here, ZEVIP, would help charge point operators by covering up to 50% of eligible project expenses for most projects, and up to 75% of projects led by indigenous developers with caps of up to $2 million per project.

Canada continues to take steps to separate itself from the wild swings and economic chaos caused by America’s random tariffs, trade policies, and dumb oil wars – and building out an infrastructure that makes it easier for its citizens to give affordable Chinese EVs a chance while strengthening its relationship with the US’ biggest economic rival?

It has been revealed that I sincerely hope this promotes the idea of installing fast chargers along routes with lower populations. I live in Ottawa, driving to my home town in northern Ontario has pretty much a single fast charger, a Tesla one with short cables at the mid point about 2.25h in. 6 stalls. If that goes down, there is nothing for about 400km of a decent charging speed. They need to have alternatives to Tesla (I've been very reliant on Tesla stations and don't own a Tesla) and more stations in between the current Tesla stations. Southern Ontario for example is very well covered with fast chargers. But the market is there so companies install them. Northern Ontario, the trans Canada highway needs these chargers badly.

If Washington doesn’t see that for, “Go pound sand, eh?” that it is, then it’s truly lost the plot – but even if the “blue wave” last week was enough to shake a little sense into the folks running the show, it may already be too late to patch things up.

Elvis Presley at Home: Tour the King’s Private Life in 14 Photos, From the Heartland to Hawaii

📅 19 May 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that elvis Presley is one of those icons so permanently etched into the fabric of American popular culture that it seems, nearly half a century after his death, as if he will live forever.
  • According to recent reports, today, the museum, which encompasses Presley’s gravesite, former home, and a collection of mementos of Presley’s rock-and-roll career, stands as a stirring reminder of one man’s life, as he grew from a beloved child to poverty-stricken parents to, arguably, the most famous man in the world.
  • In a recent development, presley and his parents pose for a photo at home in Tupelo, Mississippi, circa 1945—the year before he received his first guitar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that elvis Presley is one of those icons so permanently etched into the fabric of American popular culture that it seems, nearly half a century after his death, as if he will live forever. While Presley also had homes in California, and famously lived in Germany during his stint in the US Army, it is Graceland that is most strongly associated with the late musician. The rock and roller’s Memphis residence where he lived for 20 years and where he died at the age of 42, Graceland is America’s second-most-visited residence, behind the White House. Every year, an average of 600,000 people flock to the residence turned museum, which opened to the public in 1982.

According to recent reports, today, the museum, which encompasses Presley’s gravesite, former home, and a collection of mementos of Presley’s rock-and-roll career, stands as a stirring reminder of one man’s life, as he grew from a beloved child to poverty-stricken parents to, arguably, the most famous man in the world. Below, we’re rounding up photos of the legendary musician at his (almost) equally famous home, and other places he rested his pompadoured head.

The Presleys at home in Tupelo, around 1945.

In a recent development, presley and his parents pose for a photo at home in Tupelo, Mississippi, circa 1945—the year before he received his first guitar. The future king of rock and roll was born nearby, in a two-room house built by his father, grandfather, and uncle on January 8, 1935. That house, now a museum, was repossessed three years later, and the family bounced around other homes in the area before moving to Memphis when Presley was 13 years old. There, the family lived in Lauderdale Courts, a public housing project.

Presley relaxing at 1034 Audubon Drive.

Recent findings suggest that in March 1956, riding high on the success of Presley’s first RCA single, “Heartbreak Hotel,” the family became homeowners for the very first time. A house of her own had always been Gladys’s dream, and her 21-year-old son made it a reality when he paid $29,250 for 1034 Audubon Drive, a low-rise, seven-room ranch house with four bedrooms. Gladys likened it to living in a palace. They also added a backyard pool–at the time, it was the only one on the street. While most wealthy men of his tender age might have set their parents up with a house before shimmying off to live the bachelor’s life elsewhere, this wasn’t Elvis’s style; living together as a close-knit trio was always part of his master blueprint.

Elvis Presley and a friend chat in the back yard of his house at 1034 Audubon Drive in 1956.

On their quiet, leafy street in the rapidly growing East Memphis, the Presleys were soon living the suburban dream. Things might well have stayed that way too, had Elvis’s star not reached stratospheric heights over the following months. By the summer of 1956, Elvis had recorded smash hits “Hound Dog” and “Don’t Be Cruel.” His first feature film, Love Me Tender, premiered later that year, making him a bona fide movie star.

It has been revealed that swarms of fans soon crowded the sidewalk outside the family home day and night. Elvis had initially slept in the front bedroom, which was decorated with pink floral wallpaper, but eventually moved into the master bedroom at the back of the house after fans began peering through his window for a glimpse of their idol. To restore some shred of privacy, the Presleys had a brick and metal fence installed around the property. Elvis is pictured above leaning against the railings, chatting to a friend in his backyard.

Elvis and his parents relax on the patio.

Elvis kicks his feet up alongside his parents on the Audubon Drive home’s patio in this July 1956 photo. The Presleys had moved to this upper-middle-class neighborhood just four months prior. During their residency, the family tried to fit in with their neighbors in the affluent community to the best of their ability; Gladys let local kids cool off in their newly installed pool and made them peanut butter sandwiches, while Elvis would take them for a spin on the back of his gleaming motorcycle. But it soon became clear that Elvis’s fame would put a strain on life in the area. Perhaps it was when Hollywood star Natalie Wood came to stay at the house on Audubon—which turned the street into a circus as fans gathered to watch her pose outside on Elvis’s motorcycle—or the hot dog stand that set up outside that magically appeared to feed the constant stream of fans. The final straw may have been when a helicopter landed on the vacant lot beside the house to collect Elvis, leaving the neighbors well and truly shaken up.

In a recent development, by March 1957 the Presleys had packed their bags and moved on from the house on Audubon, restoring a relative sense of peace to the quaint suburban neighborhood. The family may have spent just a year at their Audubon Drive home, but it was a pivotal chapter in Elvis’s life story, marking a transition between the transient lifestyle of his impoverished childhood and the security and permanence he would find in his next home: Graceland.

The upcoming homeowner with his hand on one of Graceland’s now iconic columns.

In a recent development, presley skyrocketed to stardom in the mid ’50s, garnering a recording contract with RCA Records. This newfound wealth meant the boy whose home was repossessed, and who lived in public housing, could now buy the lavish house of his dreams for himself and his parents. In March 1957, the 22-year-old “Hound Dog” singer paid $102,500 for Graceland, which would remain his primary residence for the rest of his life. The home had been built in 1939 on a plot of land the original owner named after his daughter, Grace; the name stuck. Here, Presley leans on one of the home’s pillars shortly after the purchase.

Elvis in wrought iron, and in the flesh, at the gates to Graceland.

The musician poses in front of Graceland’s famous wrought iron music note gate in April 1957, around the time he had it installed. Abe Saucer designed the gates—which feature life-size images of Elvis playing guitar amid musical notes—and had them custom-built by John Dillars Jr. At the time, the property spanned 13.8 acres, with the mansion clocking in at over 10,200 square feet—later, Elvis would expand it to 17,500 square feet and 23 rooms, with additions including the famous Jungle Room.

A palace fit for the king of rock and roll.

The “Burning Love” singer walks in front of Graceland, circa 1957. Early design details that Presley added to the Colonial Revival estate included a custom 15-foot-long blue metallic sofa (later reupholstered in white), a pink flagstone wall around the property, a kidney-shaped swimming pool, and a full-size soda fountain. In his initial renovations, Presley spent $500,000 (over $5 million in today’s dollars).

In a recent development, in March 1958, Presley was drafted into the US Army. He is pictured in his off-post home in Bad Nauheim, Germany, in January 1960, shortly after being promoted to sergeant. It was here that the 24-year-old singer met a 14-year-old Priscilla Beaulieu, when a friend of his who had spotted Priscilla at a restaurant brought her to a party at Presley’s place to introduce them. To this day, the home at 14 Goethestrasse is still a landmark for fans.

Elvis and his father mourning after the death of Gladys.

Elvis and his father Vernon on the steps of Graceland in August 1958, shortly after the deathof his beloved mother, Gladys. The two had been exceptionally close, and her loss was toprove a devastating turning point. Elvis had always believed that the purpose of his extraordinary success was to provide his parents with the security and comfort they had been denied during his childhood. Buying them a home, and ultimately one as grand as Graceland, had been central to that vision. But now, just as he had achieved everything he had worked for, his mother was gone. With the loss of her unwavering love and support, it was as though a curtain had fallen on Elvis’s life. The young man who had once seemed so certain of his place in the world would never quite be the same again.

Sources indicate that in March, 1960, Presley was discharged from the Army and returned home to Graceland, but it was a sadder and lonelier place, since Gladys died while he was in basic training. Here, he stands with his Rolls-Royce in front of Graceland, circa 1960. The Jailhouse Rock star had an affinity for slick cars, but it wasn’t the only mode of transportation he enjoyed at the estate. Priscilla Beaulieu, who came to visit him at Graceland in 1962 and moved in the following year, wrote in her 1985 memoir Elvis and Me that he “turned Graceland into a private playground for us all. He’d have gun-shooting contests and also ‘screaming thrill rides’ when he’d pack several people into his custom-built golf cart and race around the grounds at top speed.”.

Elvis and Priscilla were married in Las Vegas on May 1, 1967. He was 32; she was 21. Exactly nine months later, on February 1, 1968, their first and only child, Lisa Marie Presley, was born.

Priscilla and Elvis brought a tropical design aesthetic home from their vacations in Hawaii.

Sources indicate that hawaii became a bit of a home away from home for Presley following his 1961 film, Blue Hawaii. He returned often to vacation there, including in 1968, when this snapshot was taken. The “Don’t Be Cruel” singer was so inspired by the tropical locale that he added a tiki-inspired space to Graceland. Now known as the Jungle Room, the kitschy den features wood-paneled walls, green shag carpeting on the floor and ceiling, carved wooden furniture with faux fur upholstery, and a built-in rock waterfall feature.

Priscilla, Elvis, and baby Lisa Marie relax at home.

It has been revealed that the Presleys relax in Graceland’s pool area, circa 1970. He had added the kidney-shaped pool and flagstone patio to the property in 1957. This snapshot shares a relaxed, happy moment, but life with Elvis wasn’t all pool parties for Priscilla. In Elvis and Me, Priscilla wrote frankly about their controversial relationship: “When we met, I had just turned 14. The first six months I spent with him were filled with tenderness and affection. Blinded by love, I saw none of his faults or weaknesses. He was to become the passion of my life. He taught me everything: how to dress, how to walk, how to apply makeup and wear my hair, how to behave, how to return love—his way. Over the years he became my father, husband, and very nearly God.”.

Lisa Marie and her father at Graceland.

In a recent development, elvis and Lisa Marie are shown here on the porch of Graceland in the early 1970s. Lisa Marie later recalled the curious rhythms of life at the mansion. Her father was nocturnal, she explained, and the household rarely got going before about two in the afternoon. Lisa Marie remembered fondly hearing the rotary phone ring and being summoned upstairs to spend quality time with her dad in his bedroom. “I would just sit up there, and he’d talk to me and ask what I was doing while he watched one of his 17 televisions or listened to records,” she stated in her memoir, From Here to the Great Unknown, co-written with her daughter Riley Keough. On occasion, Elvis would come downstairs and take the family and their friends out for an impromptu evening at the movie theater, shutting it down so they could watch a James Bond film or The Pink Panther.

  • According to recent reports, the company is recruiting more dealers as it expands into more stock, index, commodity, and currency markets.
  • According to recent reports, bain Capital Crypto led the Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, Variational announced on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Variational raised $110 million and plans to use it to lift trading limits on Omni, its derivatives platform.

According to recent reports, the company is recruiting more dealers as it expands into more stock, index, commodity, and currency markets. Omni traders will still rely on a single counterparty to pay their gains.

According to recent reports, bain Capital Crypto led the Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, Variational announced on Nov. 18. CEO Lucas Schuermann stated in the firm’s release that stocks, indexes and commodities already accounted for more than half of Omni’s daily volume.

Sources indicate that variational mentioned that an unnamed tier-one market maker already supplies liquidity for swaps. It is seeking institutions that can quote equities, commodities and currencies around the clock.

The Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP) is Variational’s in-house market maker, which quotes a price and takes the other side when a customer trades. It can then hedge that exposure with a traditional dealer or on another venue.

More dealers can help OLP quote more markets and take on more exposure, but the customer still settles with OLP.

Recent findings suggest that at 20:10 UTC on Nov. 20, Omni’s public market table showed $94.6 million in open interest on the Nasdaq-100 swap and $57.1 million on the gold swap.

Recent findings suggest that variational had set the initial caps at about $10 million per market when the two swaps released in September. It stated then it planned to lift each cap to $50 million or more. The company put potential capacity under its initial dealer agreements at more than $1 billion across the arrangements.

According to recent reports, under the standard schedule, both swaps trade from midnight to 5 p.m. and from 6 p.m. through 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on weekdays. They close on weekends, and holidays can change trading hours.

During a closure, orders and liquidations wait until the market reopens, while around-the-clock swap trading remains a goal.

In a recent development, variational reported over $1.3 billion in Omni open interest with the round. Entropy Advisors’ on-chain dashboard highlights a series that includes OLP alongside one that counts only traders’ positions. On its traditional-markets chart, OLP’s side equals the traders’ side.

According to recent reports, omni’s public API counts both sides in the platform total and counts only traders in its per-market long and short figures. The Series B release leaves its counting basis unspecified, so lining it up with the dashboard would require matching the series and the observation time.

Each Omni trader and OLP post collateral to a separate on-chain settlement pool for that pair, and a vault holds USDC to supply OLP’s margin.

OLP uses its own capital when hedging outside the platform, leaving customers’ collateral in their pools.

Recent findings suggest that traders settle with the Omni Liquidity Provider. OLP can hedge separately with dealers and other external venues.

In extreme volatility or a severe liquidity squeeze, OLP’s margin problem can force a trader’s position to close.

If OLP becomes insolvent, gains that accrue from then on can go unpaid, even if the trader has realized them.

It has been revealed that the trader and OLP both post collateral to their shared on-chain pool. OLP owes the trader any gains.

The stress examples illustrate possible outcomes under Variational’s published rules.

Sources indicate that the solid line highlights the customer’s settlement relationship. The dashed line shows OLP’s separate external hedge. The selectable examples trace the outcomes described in Variational’s documentation.

The stress examples illustrate possible outcomes under Variational’s published rules.

According to recent reports, if OLP cannot safely maintain margin in an extremely volatile market or needs to free up margin during a severe liquidity squeeze, its counterparty liquidation rules allow a forced close. The position closes for both sides at the settlement price even if the trader has kept up their own margin.

It has been revealed that variational claims customers’ posted collateral stays in the protocol if an outside venue loses OLP’s funds. If OLP itself becomes insolvent, gains that accrue from then on can go unpaid, including gains a trader has realized on Omni.

Police charge another Tesla driver caught asleep in rush hour as cases pile up

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A Tesla driver caught asleep behind the wheel on Ottawa’s Highway 417 during Tuesday’s rush hour now faces a careless driving charge from the Ontario Provincial Police.
  • It has been revealed that the charge carries a $490 fine and six demerit points on conviction.
  • OPP East Region posted about the stop Wednesday morning.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A Tesla driver caught asleep behind the wheel on Ottawa’s Highway 417 during Tuesday’s rush hour now faces a careless driving charge from the Ontario Provincial Police. The photo OPP shared demonstrates a latest-generation Model Y in traffic.

It has been revealed that the charge carries a $490 fine and six demerit points on conviction. It’s at least the fifth time this year Canadian police have gone public with a sleeping Tesla driver, and it’s not a coincidence that it’s happening as “Full Self-Driving” gets better.

OPP East Region posted about the stop Wednesday morning. Police didn’t name the brand or the driver-assist system, but the message was clear: “even though your vehicle has an autonomous driving feature, drivers are still required to pay due care and attention when behind the wheel.”.

According to OPP, the officer could see the driver’s eyes were closed and hands were off the steering wheel. Instead of lighting up the cruiser, police pulled in close to capture body camera footage first.

Careless driving isn’t a parking ticket in Ontario. The $490 is the set fine, but if the case goes to court, the Highway Traffic Act allows fines up to $2,000, up to six months in jail, and a licence suspension of up to two years.

Ottawa is the latest, but British Columbia has been dealing with this all year:.

This isn’t upcoming in Canada either. Back in 2020, Alberta RCMP went further and criminally charged a Tesla driver caught sleeping on Autopilot at 150 km/h with dangerous driving.

Sources indicate that the U.S. has the same problem with less enforcement. In September, Colorado State Patrol got a report of a sleeping Tesla driver on I-70 near Georgetown and never found the car. The same month, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi pressed the DOT after NBC News found 43 videos of drivers apparently asleep in moving Teslas, 17 of them posted in 2026 alone.

Recent findings suggest that and in October, a driver told CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove into a closed crash scene and hit a patrol car in Fairfield, California. Two officers were seriously injured.

Sources indicate that A few years ago, FSD needed an intervention every few miles, so nobody was napping. You couldn’t.

Now FSD can handle long highway stretches without a takeover, and that’s exactly when supervision breaks down. A human asked to watch a system that’s right 99% of the time stops watching. That’s automation complacency, and it’s one of the most studied problems in aviation and driving research.

Recent findings suggest that waymo learned this the hard way. In 2013, Google let employees use its highway driver-assist prototype and caught people falling asleep at highway speed. It decided a system that works most of the time but still needs a human to catch its mistakes was the worst of both worlds, and it went straight to driverless.

In a recent development, tesla went the other way. It sells a Level 2 system called “Full Self-Driving” that’s good enough to lull people to sleep, and it puts the full responsibility on the human who’s now asleep.

Since FSD v12.4, Tesla has relied mainly on the cabin camera above the rearview mirror to make sure the driver is watching the road. But look at what Tesla’s own owner’s manual states about it: the camera “does not require full visibility of the driver’s eyes in order to monitor attentiveness,” and the system “is still active, for example, if the driver is wearing sunglasses.”.

In other words, it’s often judging head position, not whether your eyes are open. When it can’t see your hands, it falls back to asking for a bit of torque on the wheel, which a sleeping driver resting a hand on the rim can provide.

The penalties are soft too. Five “strikeouts” suspend FSD for a week, and each strike is forgiven after three and a half days.

It has been revealed that and Tesla has been moving in the wrong direction. Musk noted in December 2025 that FSD v14.2.1 lets drivers text “depending on context of surrounding traffic.” In May 2026, he said v14.3.3 “nags less too.” When the car does detect drowsiness, Tesla’s alert reads “Drowsiness detected. Stay focused with FSD.” That pushes a tired driver to lean harder on the system instead of pulling over.

Compare that with GM’s Super Cruise, which uses a steering column camera with infrared LEDs to track head and eye position, and only works hands-free on pre-mapped highways.

Sources indicate that the Ottawa driver had their eyes closed and their hands off the wheel in rush hour traffic, and the car was still driving when an officer pulled up beside it. Whatever Tesla’s camera was checking from a foot away, it hadn’t stopped the car before a cop in the next lane did.

We’re glad Canadian police are treating this seriously. A $490 fine and six points is a real deterrent, and OPP’s message is the right one: no matter what Tesla calls it, you’re the driver.

People have been falling asleep at the wheel since driving started; many, if not most, have ended up in tragedy. At least with the self-driving cars, there is a margin of safety, especially for other drivers. These cars should monitor the driver better and pull off the road when it happens.

It has been revealed that but police can’t ticket their way out of this. These drivers aren’t edge cases anymore. They’re the predictable result of a system that drives well enough to make people relax, sold under a name that tells them relaxing is fine.

In a recent development, the fix is on Tesla’s side, and it isn’t complicated. Detect closed eyes, even behind sunglasses, which is what infrared eye-tracking is built for. When a driver doesn’t respond, slow down and pull over immediately instead of escalating warnings for minutes. Stop telling drowsy drivers to “stay focused with FSD.” And make the strike system actually sting.

NHTSA already forced a recall of over 2 million Teslas in December 2023 over weak Autopilot monitoring. Three years later, people are still sleeping through rush hour on FSD.

  • Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media.
  • That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.
  • Industry observers note that link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media. According to the service provider Bitly, its hyperlinks in older tweets from many companies, politicians, and even government accounts are now redirecting to “content unrelated to the original posts.”.

That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.

Industry observers note that link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds. The service typically works by pinning a website’s lengthy, complex URL address to a tidied-up, abbreviated shortcut in a digital registry. This shortened address then redirects anyone who clicks it to their intended online destination.

Well…in theory. Security analysts have tried to warn people about an problem known as “bit rot” for decades. In 2009—about one year after Bitly’s debut—Silicon Valley entrepreneur Joshua Schacter wrote a prescient blog post cautioning against what he felt were potentially serious flaws in the link-shortening “middleman” system. Amid the issues, Schacter cited a “newly introduced and potentially unreliable” tool that ties an original hyperlink to the “health of a third party.”.

It has been revealed that “The shortener may decide a link is a Terms Of Service violation and delete it. If the shortener accidentally erases a database, forgets to renew its domain, or just disappears, the link will break,” he explained. “If a top-level domain changes its policy on commercial use, the link will break. If the shortener gets hacked, every link becomes a potential phishing attack.”.

Recent findings suggest that it now appears bad actors recently identified countless of these Bitly links previously posted across social media between 2009 and 2014. Although their exact methods aren’t clear, it’s possible they generated their own custom Bitly links using the addresses in the social media posts, then used those to send people to different destinations. Bitly says its links do not automatically expire, but paid owners may redirect existing links.

According to recent reports, many examples were found among the more than 60,000 posts on X from President Donald Trump’s official account. In one of Trump’s previous posts about his golf course in Scotland, the Bitly link temporarily redirected to Wikipedia’s entry on the Epstein Files. Targets also included corporations like McDonald’s, with one of the fast food giant’s 2011 Bitly URLs suddenly linked to Wikipedia’s page about the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

Not every hijacked post funneled people to upsetting outcomes. Instead of a cybersecurity PSA, the Bitly address in a 2021 post from the FBI briefly linked to a photo of a blubbery seal. Another of Trump’s URLs sent you to the popular video game, Geometry Dash.

In its acknowledgement of the problem on November 15, Bitly reported it had identified and suspended the bad actors’ accounts, and were in the process of “disabling the affected links.”.

“Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the concern and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future,” Bitly wrote at the time.

Volkswagen is turning one of its best-selling nameplates into an electric SUV. The upcoming ID. Tiguan is now rolling off the assembly line and will replace the ID.4 in 2027.

Industry observers note that the ID.4 and ID.5 are on the way out, and the new ID. Tiguan will replace them in Volkswagen’s EV lineup next year.

Following the ID. Polo and ID. Cross, which are now on sale in Europe, the ID. Tiguan is the next model to go on sale as a “True Volkswagen,” as the company calls it.

The newly introduced electric SUV adopts Volkswagen’s best-selling nameplate, the Tiguan, as part of its shift away from the numerical system used on the outgoing ID.4 and ID.5.

Sources indicate that volkswagen announced on Thursday that series production of the electric ID. Tiguan has now begun at its Embden Plant in Germany.

It has been revealed that “The Tiguan is our best-selling model worldwide, and the ID.4 and ID.5 are among our most successful electric cars,” VW Brand CEO Thomas Shafer mentioned last month after unveiling the upcoming SUV. He added that “The ID. Tiguan brings these two success stories together.”.

The ID. Tiguan will be a step change from its predecessors, the ID.4 and ID.5, featuring Volkswagen’s “Pure Positive” design language, which includes an overhauled interior and exterior design and updated tech.

According to recent reports, volkswagen said the ID. Tiguan’s “hallmark feature” is the completely redesigned exterior. The latest design remains closer to the gas-powered Tiguan, with a boxy, traditional SUV look.

Recent findings suggest that unlike the ID.4’s aerodynamic design, the upcoming ID. Tiguan features a wide, chunky front end and traditional pull-style door handles instead of the flush ones.

Industry observers note that in Volkswagen’s words, the newly introduced ID. Tiguan electric SUV “looks like a vehicle from the premium segment.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

That's what Binance told customers to expect while it reviews deposits from MEXC. Try to move money the other way, and Binance says it'll refuse to send it in the first place.

The US order barring covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC takes effect Dec. 10, but Binance confirmed its policy a month earlier and cited the Treasury's finding.

MEXC can keep matching buy and sell orders in the markets it still serves, while one of the world's largest exchanges has already told traders it will restrict what they can move between the two.

On Nov. 6, the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) found that MEXC was a foreign financial institution of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.

The agency acted under Section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, and its order in the Federal Register prohibits transfers to and from MEXC through covered US financial institutions.

Industry observers note that the prohibition has no scheduled end and covers MEXC's foreign operations and successor entities. It reaches crypto as well as conventional money, and FinCEN names Bitcoin explicitly.

Foreign financial firms can make dollar payments through banks that hold accounts with US banks, an arrangement known as correspondent banking.

Recent findings suggest that finCEN considered restricting those accounts but concluded that doing so would leave other kinds of transfers untouched. Instead, it chose to prohibit transfers that pass through a covered institution, even when MEXC has no account with the institution handling the payment.

Exchanges and payment providers outside that group may adopt their own restrictions, but those policies require separate confirmation.

It has been revealed that finCEN estimates that MEXC handled at least $16.7 billion in likely illicit activity in the five years through May 2026. The agency's figures include about $129 million it says MEXC directly facilitated with Garantex after the Russian crypto exchange was sanctioned, and about $4.1 million involving its successor, Grinex, after it too was sanctioned.

FinCEN also cites transfers linked to Iran and North Korea, along with proceeds from cybercrime. The agency acknowledges that legitimate customers use MEXC and indicates the financial risks it identified warrant restricting transfers involving the exchange itself.

In its Nov. 7 public response, MEXC said it was operating normally, and customer assets remained secure. It said it had opened an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls and intended to engage with regulators.

Reports noted net outflows from tracked MEXC wallets after the announcement.

Binance can refuse to send a withdrawal because it controls the account the money would leave.

Yet, when crypto comes from another platform, the network can process the transaction without asking the recipient's permission.

FinCEN acknowledges that limitation in the order, and Binance's notice reveals what the exchange can do once the funds arrive: it can withhold credit while it reviews the transfer and potentially restrict or close the customer's Binance account.

Any funds left at MEXC stay in that account unless the customer moves them separately.

Recent findings suggest that an on-chain confirmation and exchange-account credit are separate events. Binance notes deposits from MEXC entities are withheld for review, while outgoing requests are declined.

Blockchain settlement does not force a receiving exchange to credit a customer balance.

In a recent development, binance describes platform policy, not a documented individual incident. FinCEN binds covered US financial institutions. A confirmed blockchain transaction does not guarantee immediate account credit; account restrictions are possible, not certain.

In a recent development, based on the Binance notice published November 10, 2026, and the FinCEN order published November 10 with a December 10 effective date. Inbound path is illustrative; no verified individual customer transfer is claimed.

The business risk for exchanges becomes more serious if customers and professional market makers, the firms that keep buy and sell orders available, lose more ways to fund their accounts or move out the proceeds.

Moving balances between exchanges is part of how those firms keep money available where they need it.

MEXC claims changes at third-party issuers ended its Asia-Pacific card program on Nov. 11 and its Global Card on Nov. 18.

According to recent reports, global Card customers can no longer use their cards for purchases. MEXC indicates it will credit balances left on the cards to customers' spot accounts within three business days of a Nov. 21 snapshot.

That would leave customers with an exchange balance rather than a working payment card, because spending it with a card requires an issuer.

In France, MEXC had announced its wind-down in October, before the Treasury acted. Its schedule for French accounts stopped euro deposits and withdrawals on Nov. 18, while crypto withdrawals remain available until March 5, 2027.

Recent findings suggest that trading restrictions begin in batches, and French accounts enter withdrawal-only mode on Jan. 25.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 20, DefiLlama displayed more than $1 billion in MEXC spot trading over 24 hours. That figure measures trading across the platform, including customers outside France, and indicates little about whether an individual French account can accept deposits, place fresh orders, or withdraw its remaining funds.

It has been revealed that after Dec. 10, the practical reach of FinCEN's order will depend partly on which banks and exchanges handle a trader's money and which restrictions those firms apply.

Industry observers note that binance has already told customers how it intends to handle MEXC transfers. Other firms may take different approaches, which traders will discover when they try to withdraw a balance, deposit it somewhere else, or spend it through a payment service.

Breaking: Meet SHRINCS: Bitcoin's Emerging Frontrunner for a Post-Quantum Signature

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick, with Mikhail Kudinov and collaborators, published a security analysis on Thursday for SHRINCS, advancing an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.
  • “We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, mentioned in reference to a draft of SHRINCS’ Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP).
  • Notably, SHRINCS is a hash-based signature scheme that leverages SHA-256 to anchor its security in battle-tested primitives that are already used by Bitcoin, representing a conservative effort to minimize the proposal’s trust assumptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick, with Mikhail Kudinov and collaborators, published a security analysis on Thursday for SHRINCS, advancing an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.

“We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, mentioned in reference to a draft of SHRINCS’ Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP). “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.".

Notably, SHRINCS is a hash-based signature scheme that leverages SHA-256 to anchor its security in battle-tested primitives that are already used by Bitcoin, representing a conservative effort to minimize the proposal’s trust assumptions.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

According to recent reports, that said, the scheme comes with trade-offs, most notably by introducing potential security vulnerabilities at the implementation level if misused. The scheme combines two spending paths: a small, more efficient stateful signature option and a larger, more costly stateless path with fewer security risks on the implementation side.

In a recent development, although stateful signatures are compact, preserving Bitcoin’s ability to process transactions efficiently, a user can trigger a critical failure—where an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal funds if a one-time state is accidentally reused. Because SHRINCS’ stateful path relies on one-time keys that can only safely sign a single transaction, wallet developers must carefully track each key’s state.

Recent findings suggest that “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” Nick told Head of MARA Foundation Isabel Foxen Duke during a recent appearance on MARA Foundation TV. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”.

According to Nick, for SHRINCS to work safely in the real world, its specification and corresponding wallet implementations must automatically enforce the stateless path fallback in any situation where a state counter could possibly be compromised.

While some owners might gravitate toward stateless signatures out of caution, Nick warns that widespread adoption could bloat the blockchain and drive up fees across the network.

Bitcoin’s current ECDSA signatures are typically 71 bytes long (and Taproot Schnorr signatures are 64 bytes). Under SHRINCS, stateful signatures are anywhere from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while stateless ones are 5,777 bytes. That said, optimizations of both signature paths have been accelerating with the support of AI-based research, Nick noted.

It has been revealed that “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very massive signatures,” he remarked. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”.

As the SHRINCS working group—which includes researchers backed by nonprofits including Brink and OpenSats—continues to refine the proposal’s specification, Blockstream researchers stress that getting the cryptographic foundation right is only half the battle.

In a recent development, whether the broader Bitcoin ecosystem is ready to embrace SHRINCS’ inherent trade-offs will depend heavily on feedback from the network’s stakeholders in the months ahead. Meanwhile, Nick and Kudinov are requesting review of the proposal and the security analysis.

THE MOST CONVENIENT travel companion is a backpack, and I envy those who can pack a trip’s worth of clothing into one. But I need a carry-on suitcase; I like to think of it as option packing instead of overpacking. For years I relied on my Filson Duffle—and still love it as a weekender—but found myself wanting a roller bag for hands-free travel and to get a little more organization.

According to recent reports, carry-on suitcases are quite bland though. They’re plastic boxes that require you to attach a keychain or bandana just to recognize your own. I considered Rimowa’s iconic carry-ons for a short while until I remembered my tax bracket and came back to reality (if you’re unfamiliar, they’re expensive). More palatable aluminum options from Away and Monos exist, but they miss the mark for me, be it style or features.

A lucky typo while searching Porter Yoshida bags led me to Portar luggage. The brand’s aluminum and polycarbonate/aluminum luggage is sleek, durable, and costs a fifth of a Rimowa cabin bag. I used the Portar Aluminum Carry-On Luggage all summer and it exceeded my expectations, and it’s now seeing me through holiday travel.

Portar’s carry-on is exactly what I was looking for lookswise—an unbranded aluminum suitcase with leather handles. Functionally, it surpassed expectations after trips to Michigan, Chicago, Houston, and Amsterdam.

Recent findings suggest that the aluminum shell has held up to TSA's less-than-careful hands over the past couple of months. Aluminum luggage gathers minor dings and scuffs throughout travel—it’s part of the charm—but the black covers any marks I may have picked up, and I don’t notice any. I also like the rivets along the shell's border. It reminds me of old travel trunks I’ve seen in vintage stores.

According to recent reports, the leather handles are not only a nice aesthetic touch, but they actually make handling the suitcase much easier. They’re substantial and padded, unlike the flimsy plastic strip you see on a lot of carry-on luggage. It makes hoisting it into the overhead cabin a bit more steady and secure.

In a recent development, the latches are also a huge change for me, as I’m used to hassling with zippers that snag or tear—I will never go back to zippered luggage again. Both the telescopic handle and wheels operate smoothly, so I glide gracefully to my gate.

Technically my fiancée’s Away carry-on has more space based on dimensions, but I swear I can efficiently pack more into my Portar. Maybe it’s the clever pocket configuration or the removable compression straps and divider, but coming back from Amsterdam, we were counting on my Portar to bring back Delft ceramics and other acquisitions. All of which fit despite my over (option!) packing.

My Portar will now accompany me home for the holidays. It will also travel to the Pitztal Valley in Austria, then on to Vienna the week after Thanksgiving. It’s a first-class carry-on in the cabin space above my economy seat. Air travel used to be luxurious, and people would dress up for the occasion of reaching 38,000 feet. The Portar carry-on is bringing back some of that charm and costs me less than $300.

Latest Update: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam delay reveals a troubling pattern behind its biggest network upgrades

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.
  • Industry observers note that on Nov.
  • In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached new highs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 20, Ethereum Foundation researcher Toni Wahrstätter stated the upgrade, which the foundation had targeted for the first half of 2026, cannot reach mainnet before mid-January 2027, after delays disrupted its testing schedule.

In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached new highs.

“Nobody did a bad job, but I think we fooled ourselves, twice.”.

His findings show that Glamsterdam was assigned the shortest development timeline in years despite being Ethereum's most ambitious upgrade by several measures.

According to Wahrstätter, monthly contributions to Ethereum's technical specifications have increased between twofold and 3.5-fold since 2024, reflecting a substantial acceleration in development activity.

The improvement has extended to testing. Glamsterdam completed 12 development networks, or devnets, in 160 days, compared with seven devnets over 285 days for Pectra, an earlier Ethereum upgrade.

However, Wahrstätter argued that the acceleration has created another problem: developers can now produce specifications, code and tests faster than their colleagues can review them and understand their implications.

Sources indicate that that challenge has become more pronounced with Glamsterdam's unprecedented size. The upgrade contains approximately 6,080 lines of execution-layer specifications, compared with 2,318 for Prague, the previous record.

In a separate count of proposal specifications, Wahrstätter put two of Glamsterdam's most vital changes, enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS) and block-level access lists (BALs), at approximately 11,900 and 9,300 lines, respectively. The other 16 proposals collectively represent about 3,600 lines.

The complexity is also reflected in EIP-8037, a proposal that changes how Ethereum charges for creating fresh blockchain state. Although its specifications contain roughly 1,700 lines, the proposal requires approximately 30,000 lines of tests, more than any other proposal included in the upgrade.

Together, this illustrates why faster code production has failed to produce a corresponding acceleration in network upgrades.

Industry observers note that indeed, Wahrstätter's historical analysis demonstrated that every Ethereum upgrade since Dencun has taken more than 400 days from finalizing its scope to reaching mainnet. For context, the three most recent upgrades took between 433 and 475 days, even though their technical scope was smaller than Glamsterdam's.

Despite that record, Glamsterdam was given a development target of just 320 days, substantially shorter than the timelines achieved by previous upgrades.

Industry observers note that wahrstätter found that virtually every Ethereum upgrade with an revealed target had missed its deadline. Fusaka was the exception, but only after developers removed Ethereum Object Format (EOF), a major component originally planned for inclusion.

Pectra similarly required developers to divide its original scope across separate upgrades.

It has been revealed that glamsterdam took a different approach. Developers kept adding proposals to successive testing environments while work on its two main components, ePBS and BALs, continued.

Unlike earlier upgrades, the team made no comparable reduction in scope to protect its development timeline.

Consequently, Glamsterdam reached public testing before its specifications had stabilized, creating additional work at a stage when developers would ordinarily be preparing for deployment.

Wahrstätter's analysis showed that Ethereum upgrades between Altair and Deneb recorded no specification changes after their first public testnet.

Pectra recorded two changes, while Fusaka recorded one. Glamsterdam registered 10 in just six weeks.

The difference also appeared in client development. Work on Pectra declined substantially after public testing began, whereas Glamsterdam-related activity increased 34% following its Sepolia activation, alongside a 25% rise in client commits.

Those late changes became particularly consequential after security researchers identified problems involving EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, which alter how Ethereum charges for certain operations.

The proposals could disrupt assumptions embedded in existing smart contracts, prompting developers to postpone Glamsterdam's Oct. 26 activation on the Hoodi testnet.

The setback has pushed Glamsterdam's expected interval between its first public testnet and mainnet activation beyond 100 days, compared with the 4- to 10-week window typical of previous upgrades, according to Wahrstätter.

According to recent reports, during their Nov. 19 meeting, Ethereum developers tentatively targeted Dec. 16 or 17 for Hoodi testing, with mid-January 2027 emerging as the earliest possible mainnet date if the specification stays unchanged.

Wahrstätter argued that preventing further delays would require developers to base release targets on historical performance and set firm deadlines for dropping unfinished features and completing specifications before public testing begins.

He also questioned treating successful devnet deployments as evidence that proposals were sufficiently mature for inclusion in an upgrade. He said:.

“I'm sure we can ship faster, but for that, we must ship smaller.”.

Recent findings suggest that the next decision comes Nov. 26, when Ethereum's core developers are expected to determine whether Glamsterdam can proceed with its proposed December Hoodi activation.

A further postponement would place additional pressure on a release schedule that has already extended well beyond its original target.

How a Former New York City Caviar Factory Became an Art-Filled Oasis of Calm

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it’s late Friday afternoon in Manhattan and Alexis Piqueras has misplaced his phone.
  • According to recent reports, A break from our harried digital world was what he was seeking when, not long ago, he set out to buy an apartment downtown, having returned to New York after a three-year stint in Los Angeles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s late Friday afternoon in Manhattan and Alexis Piqueras has misplaced his phone. Not that he’s concerned. Bathed in the light of October’s early setting sun, the Spanish-born producer and founder of AP Studio, settles into a Charlotte Perriand dining chair at his Tribeca apartment. The vibe is calm: a mix of warm hues, rich textures, and timeworn woods. Candles perfume the air. And all around us the faces and limbs of figurative artworks seem to join our conversation. “I’ll find it eventually,” Piqueras notes, unperturbed by his absent device.

According to recent reports, A break from our harried digital world was what he was seeking when, not long ago, he set out to buy an apartment downtown, having returned to New York after a three-year stint in Los Angeles. “Sometimes I need to hide amid the chaos,” claims Piqueras, who has built a busy career collaborating with brands on the order of Louis Vuitton, Celine, and Loewe. His real-estate ambitions transcended any simple notions of an urban oasis. Yes, he wanted peace and quiet. But he also wanted some untouched architectural grit that felt true to the city, in particular his visions of its post-industrial 1970s waterfront.

Piqueras relaxes in the living area of his Manhattan loft with his dogs, Prince and Bridget; artworks by Wolfgang Tillmans (top) and Giangiacomo Rossetti.

A Harold Ancart painting and Prince preside over the entry.

Charlotte Perriand chairs and a custom sofa face off across an Alvar Aalto prototype cocktail table; floor lamp by Isamu Noguchi and seascape by Paul Thek.

Industry observers note that he found that in Tribeca. Its warehouses and sleepy streets also reminded him of his time in Berlin, where he fell in love with club culture. His newly introduced loft, located in what had once been a 19th-century caviar factory, retains its original brick walls, timber columns, and wood windows, through which he can view slices of the Hudson River. A previous renovation had made smart use of the 2,500 square feet, carving out a primary suite, guest bedroom, office, powder room and pantry alongside the open cooking/living/dining space. It all just needed to be pared back. “The moment you take away everything, you have all you need,” Piqueras says.

Industry observers note that working with the Brazilian-born furniture and interior designer Pali Xisto Cornelsen, he stripped back what time-stamped interventions had been made over the years. In the kitchen, they updated the existing high-gloss kitchen cabinetry with white-painted fronts and chunky solid-cherry pulls, also installing stainless-steel countertops and a new island, trimmed in wood. The walls were coated in Benjamin Moore’s Simply White, the floorboards refinished, and the windows dressed in linen roman shades. “I was conscious of creating a neutral canvas,” says Xisto Cornelsen, who removed all the recessed lighting. “You’re gonna feel a certain calm.”.

A David Wojnarowicz artwork hangs above a circa-1960 Knoll console.

The den features a built-in daybed; etchings by David Hockney and photograph by Nan Goldin.

In a recent development, art introduces faces to that expanse. Working with advisor Joe Sheftel to expand his collection, Piqueras has assembled a sophisticated trove with a focus on works by Queer talents of recent or current memory. Those include photographs by Wolfgang Tillmans, Peter Hujar, and Alvin Baltrop, who documented the pre-AIDS gay revelry of the nearby Hudson River piers. Elsewhere are portraits by Larry Stanton and David Hockney. Some bare bodies, Piqueras admits, have left houseguests blushing. But the intention was never skin for the sake of shock. “It’s a lot about community,” states Sheftel. “The apartment also functions that way, as a fun space for friends and play.” A romantic spirit comes across in still lives (a burning candle by Phoebe Helander) and landscapes ( a Doron Langberg painting of Fire Island Pines). Evident too is Piqueras’s deep love of New York City. “There’s also a narrative of activism—of power and creativity through crisis,” says Sheftel, pointing out works by David Wojnarowicz.

In the dining area, Charlotte Perriand chairs surround a Pierre Chapo table beneath a Paavo Tynell lamp; photograph by Wolfgang Tillmans, still life by Phoebe Helander, and portrait by Larry Stanton.

Displayed above the custom DJ station (aka Piqueras’s little Berlin) are works by Wolfgang Tilmans, Seth Baker, and Issy Wood.

A Doron Langberg painting hangs amidst the kitchen’s reimagined cabinetry; photograph by Wolfgang Tillmans and stools by Alvar Aalto.

The library features a mix of vintage Scandinavian finds, including a Märta Blomstedt lounge chair, Paavo Tynell pendant light, and a desk and side chair by Axel Einar Hjorth. The large-scale photograph is by Wolfgang Tillmans and the shelves display works by Alvin Baltrop, David Wojnarowicz, Jacob Littlejohn, Peter Hujar, and Giangiacomo Rossetti. Resting on the floor is an etching by David Hockney.

A Hunter Reynolds artwork takes pride of place above Piqueras’s bed; speakers by Ojas.

The primary bath retains the building’s original brickwork.

According to recent reports, elsewhere throughout the interiors, they added custom millwork, including the office’s daybed and wall-mounted desk, the living area’s bookshelves, and the dining area’s DJ station, a corner Piqueras calls his little Berlin. Tapered silhouettes and bevels soften edges. “There are all these happy surprises,” says Cornelsen, who referenced design heroes like Le Corbusier, Joaquim Tenreiro, and Jean Prouvé. Vintage furniture adds to that neutral rhapsody, with choice finds by Pierre Chapo, Isamu Noguchi, and Alvar Aalto, whose coffee table prototype anchors the living area. It is joined by a cast of other Scandinavian characters, among them light fixtures by Paavo Tynell, the upholstered Märta Blomstedt lounge chair where Piqueras enjoys his morning tea, and pieces by Axel Einar Hjorth.

It has been revealed that collecting and decorating, Piqueras has found, are not unlike his daily profession. “Renovating an apartment is a kind of production,” he claims. “My skill is to orchestrate.” But it’s a break from the grind that he now gets to relish at home. “Work is insane. The streets are insane. But then I can come here,” he says. “I put down my phone—and then I don’t think about it.”.

A Paavo Tynell pendant crowns the guest bedroom, which features more custom millwork and displays artworks by Precious Okoyomon (left) and Christopher Culver.

A Wolfgang Tillmans photograph takes the place of the guest bath’s vanity mirror.

A Sol LeWitt artwork rests on the den’s custom desk; photograph by Wolfgang Tillmans and chair by Axel Einar Hjorth.
